guidance: The command argument is the exact program invocation to execute. Repeat it exactly as written.
Do not substitute a workload description, add cd/setup wrappers, change python/python3, or infer a different command from surrounding context.

nodes.guidance: Express the node count clearly enough to recover the expected numeric value.

tasks.guidance: Express the task count clearly enough to recover the expected numeric value.

time_limit.guidance: Express the time limit clearly enough to recover the expected value; exact spelling is helpful but not required.

job_name.guidance: Job names are identifiers; preserve the expected job_name exactly.

working_directory.guidance: Working directories are paths; preserve the expected working_directory exactly.

guidance: Flux scheduler/resource arguments such as nodes, tasks, time_limit, job_name, and working_directory are separate tool arguments. They are not part of command unless already present in the expected command string.

run_info_json.guidance: run_info_json is a literal JSON string argument. Preserve that string exactly when it is included in a generated prompt.

job_id.guidance: job_id is the local MADA tracking identifier. Do not replace it with flux_job_id.

styles.description: A normal conversational request from a capable user.
A short command-like request with minimal extra wording.
A beginner-style request that uses informal wording and may over-explain.
An underspecified casual request, but still containing enough information to imply the expected tool call.
An explicit instruction naming the intended server, tool, and key arguments.

prompts.text: Use the Flux server submit_command tool for one single ad hoc command. Set command to "python -V", nodes=1, tasks=1, time_limit=15m, job_name=python_version, and working_directory=/tmp/mada_flux_eval/single_command. Do not use submit_jobs or any generated run manifest.

Please submit one ad hoc Flux command, not a generated run manifest. Run python -V from /tmp/mada_flux_eval/single_command with one node, one total task, a 15 minute time limit, and job name python_version.
Flux submit_command single command: command="python -V", nodes=1, tasks=1, time_limit=15m, job_name=python_version, working_directory=/tmp/mada_flux_eval/single_command.

Use Flux submit_command for one single ad hoc command. Run command "python simulate.py --case fluid_test --steps 10" with nodes=2, tasks=8, time_limit=30m, job_name=fluid_test_eval, and working_directory=/tmp/mada_flux_eval/fluid_test_job. This is not a generated-runs manifest.

I need one ad hoc Flux command submission, not submit_jobs. Launch python simulate.py --case fluid_test --steps 10 from /tmp/mada_flux_eval/fluid_test_job, request two nodes and eight total tasks, cap it at 30 minutes, and name the job fluid_test_eval.
Flux submit_command: command="python simulate.py --case fluid_test --steps 10", nodes=2, tasks=8, time_limit=30m, job_name=fluid_test_eval, working_directory=/tmp/mada_flux_eval/fluid_test_job.
Use Flux check_job_status with the local MADA tracking field job_id set to job_000123. Do not use flux_job_id.
Please look up the current Flux status for the local MADA tracking ID job_000123. Use check_job_status with job_id, not flux_job_id.
Check Flux job status for all tracked jobs. Do not pass job_id or flux_job_id.
Show me the status of every Flux job the server is tracking right now. This is the all-jobs status query, so do not include job_id or flux_job_id.
Flux check_job_status for all tracked jobs, no job_id, no flux_job_id.

Use Flux submit_jobs for generated runs. Pass this exact literal JSON string as run_info_json: {"runs":[{"id":"run_001","run_location":"/tmp/mada_flux_eval/run_001","command":"simulate_case","args":["--input","case1.deck"]},{"id":"run_002","run_location":"/tmp/mada_flux_eval/run_002","command":"simulate_case","args":["--input","case2.deck"]}]}. Leave blocking at its default async behavior; do not ask Flux to wait for completion.

Please submit these generated runs through Flux using submit_jobs, not submit_command. The run manifest has run_001 in /tmp/mada_flux_eval/run_001 with simulate_case --input case1.deck and run_002 in /tmp/mada_flux_eval/run_002 with simulate_case --input case2.deck. Use the default non-blocking async submission behavior.

Use Flux submit_jobs for generated runs and set blocking=true so the tool waits until all runs finish. Pass this exact literal JSON string as run_info_json: {"runs":[{"id":"run_sync_001","run_location":"/tmp/mada_flux_eval/run_sync_001","command":"simulate_case","args":["--input","sync1.deck"]},{"id":"run_sync_002","run_location":"/tmp/mada_flux_eval/run_sync_002","command":"simulate_case","args":["--input","sync2.deck"]}]}.

Submit these generated runs through Flux with submit_jobs and wait until all runs finish before returning. The run manifest includes run_sync_001 at /tmp/mada_flux_eval/run_sync_001 with simulate_case --input sync1.deck and run_sync_002 at /tmp/mada_flux_eval/run_sync_002 with simulate_case --input sync2.deck. This should be the blocking=true case.
